page: Amazon Web Services r6a.2xlarge is an AMD-powered, memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, providing 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance offers 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The system provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps, does not include local disk storage, and contains no integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show balanced computational characteristics with specific strengths. The instance recorded a strong single-core stress-ng CPU score of 2,993.58, placing in the top quartile, alongside an average multi-core score of 11,963.47 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,369.0. In-memory operations yielded 8.95 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations score of 3,798.75. However, uncached memory bandwidth represents a performance tradeoff, with large-block 256MB read and write speeds falling into the bottom quartile at 35.55 GB/s and 19.54 GB/s respectively.

By leveraging third-generation AMD EPYC processors, the r6a.2xlarge provides a cost-efficient alternative within the AWS memory-optimized category compared to traditional x86 counterparts. The dense 64.0 GB memory footprint supports memory-bound applications without requiring over-provisioning of CPU cores, though reliance on external network storage must be considered for data persistence. This instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, medium-scale relational databases, and enterprise data processing jobs.
